title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint and struck through with long diagonal strokes, so it is a cancelled sheet. What can be made out, together with its layout, matches the previous page almost line for line. Legible fragments include: 'Lorsque ... dans C les produits fibrés existent, alors il n'y a pas de différence entre épim. eff. et épim. stricts ... quatre (au lieu de cinq) variantes ...'; then 'Prop. 0 ...'; then 'Prop. 1 Conditions équivalentes', with 'a) Pour tout X ∈ Ob C ...' and 'b) Pour tout X ∈ Ob C, considérant G/X → C ... lim T → X'. Near the bottom there are a few further lines, apparently continuing into the proof or a remark ('... différence ...'). It is either a crossed-out earlier draft or a faint duplicate/show-through of the preceding page.

The mathematics is elementary category theory, preparatory to the Galois/motivic material. In a category C with fibre products:
- Effective and strict epimorphic families coincide.
- The variants of 'épimorphicité' for families reduce from five to four.
- These properties can be tested on the sieve (crible) generated by the family.
- They are stable under enlarging the family.

Prop. 1 concerns a set G of objects and the full subcategory it generates. The following are equivalent:
- (a) For every X, the family of all arrows G_i → X with source in G is epimorphic (resp. strictly epimorphic).
- (b) The canonical map colim_{T ∈ G/X} T → X, read through representables (lim h_Y(T) versus h_Y(X)), is a monomorphism (resp. an isomorphism).

In modern terms, G is a generating family (resp. a strong/dense generator). 'Strictly epimorphic for all X' is the statement that G is a dense subcategory, i.e. X is the canonical colimit of the objects of G mapping to it. The context is the formalism of Galois categories and fibre functors leading to the Galois theory of motives. The next page begins a new topic: commutative class field theory as motives with commutative ('metabelian') motivic fundamental groups.
errors: No mathematical errors are checkable on this page: it is cancelled and largely illegible.

As stated on the previous page, the 'resp.' case of Prop. 1 is correct: a family of all maps from G to X being strictly epimorphic for all X is exactly the density condition X ≅ colim_{G/X} T in the representable sense.

ideas.what: Coincidence of effective and strict epimorphic families in categories with fibre products; testing via the generated sieve.

The headings read 'Prop. 0' and 'Prop. 1 Conditions équivalentes', not 'Rem. 0' / 'Rem. 1'.
